native_result.query: How does the effect of increasing education expenditure on per capita GDP compare between developing countries and countries in Sub-Saharan Africa?
native_result.HypoA: The effect of increasing education expenditure on per capita GDP is more pronounced in developing countries outside of Sub-Saharan Africa compared to those within it
native_result.HypoB: The association between education expenditure (% of GNI) and per-capita income (GNI per capita, 2015 US$) differs significantly between the two groups in the balanced 2011-2015 window: it is strongly negative in Lower-Middle-Income/developing countries (a one-SD ~0.2pp-of-GNI higher share is associated with ~13% lower per-capita income; slope -0.135, SE 0.018, p<0.001) but near zero in Sub-Saharan Africa (~2% lower; slope -0.021). The group difference (interaction +0.114 log-points, SE 0.018, p<0.001) survives controls (secondary enrollment, export growth) and lagged education expenditure. This is a conditional association, not a causal effect: no instruments exist, the negative sign largely reflects the mechanical denominator effect (income outpacing nominal education spending), and SSA income is observed for only 5 years.
native_result.WorkflowB: Reshape wide CSV to long panel; use balanced 2011-2015 window (n=10); standardize edu_exp; pooled OLS log(GNIpc) ~ z(edu) + SSA + z(edu)xSSA with HC1 robust SEs; per-group simple regressions; limited-control models (secondary enrollment, exports); lagged-edu robustness; LMC 1975-2015 long-panel validation (trend, Durbin-Watson, AR(1), window-vs-full slope comparison); descriptive spending->enrollment mechanism.
